notes: This source/test traceability contract covers only Umbra's bounded non-regional timestamped Delete Object Instance and timestamped Remove Object Instance path in the non-installable 2025 development profile. It exercises lower-bound validation, pending-delete retraction with object reconstitution, exact-bound callback delivery before Time Advance Grant, official timestamp/order/retraction fields, the supplied tag and producing federate, and sender callback exclusion. A cross-service target-departure regression additionally proves that a time-6 removal commits object departure before a separately queued time-7 directed interaction reaches its callback boundary, where the stale directed payload is suppressed. Focused Connection Lost regressions additionally retain time-5 and time-6 removals accepted from the lost regulator through its configured unconditional-divest cleanup until the surviving constrained federate receives Remove Object Instance before its matching time-6 grant; one counterpart keeps the cutoff marker and object state live for a second survivor that requests time 6 only after the first callback, while the DELETE_OBJECTS companion preserves the same timestamped lifecycle rather than replacing it with automatic receive-order removal. A separate mixed nonconstrained/time-constrained scenario now proves a legal post-delivery Retract: a delivered recipient receives Request Retraction, still-pending fanout is withdrawn, and an execution-owned invocation snapshot restores the object, name, known-instance state, and committed split attribute ownership before that callback is exposed. A matching three-member local-delete companion proves that recipient-local forget suppresses only one queued Remove Object Instance while an independent survivor receives the removal before its own grant. A second scenario confirms an owner who resigns after delivered removal is not revived or notified, while its former attribute remains unowned. The bounded tombstone lifecycle now retains a lightweight terminal record for MessageCanNoLongerBeRetracted while it releases heavyweight deletion payload/snapshot and the deleted-instance marker only after no still-joined recipient remains pending. A focused no-recipient case proves the name is then available for a fresh named registration. A new save/restore terminal-deletion case saves that lightweight tombstone after the object/name has been reclaimed, creates a distinct post-save deletion, restores the saved image, and preserves the saved classification while rejecting the post-save handle and object name. Accepted producer TAR/TARA/NMR/NMRA/FQR requests, immediate actual-lookahead increases, successful Retract, and producer resignation are wired to that lifecycle. A separately contracted ordinary lifecycle case queues one removal across a Time Constrained disable and callback-gated re-enable, then proves one Remove Object Instance callback before the matching grant with the original metadata and terminal retraction classification. A separately contracted save/restore case saves that live queued removal, makes the designator terminal after saving, restores the snapshot, delivers the original removal through FQR, and then exercises post-delivery Request Retraction with object/name reconstitution. Complete alternate-advance, broader re-enable, active in-flight ownership, other producer/recipient resignation, remote transport, packaging, catalog evidence, and conformance remain outside this slice.
